claim: random_forest is the strongest single model (0.8287 CV)
note: Measured on 3 identical passes; deterministic given the frozen data and fixed seed.

claim: Soft-vote ensemble does NOT beat the best single model
note: 0.8273 vs 0.8287. Well inside the +/-0.015-0.030 fold spread, so 'tied' is the honest reading, not 'worse'.

claim: knn is clearly the weakest model (0.7879) and is a poor ensemble member
logistic leaves 9 hyperparameters at their defaults; only C is tuned
note: make introspect --show-untuned lists them. Widening this search is the cheapest untried lever.

claim: hist_gradient_boosting leaves 16 parameters at defaults; only 2 are tuned
note: Largest untuned surface of any model here.

claim: No model has been tried with engineered features beyond the 12 current ones
note: explore proposed Title, Deck, FamilySize, IsAlone, AgeMissing; all are in use. Nothing newer has been proposed.

claim: select_members crossed experiment boundaries, contaminating the val score
note: It filtered on frozen_sha256 but not experiment_id, so exp-002 ensembled members tuned by the pre-container baseline on all 712 rows -- including exp-002's own 143 validation rows. Its 0.8392 was a selection statistic, not a measurement. Fixed by scoping select_members to the open experiment; exp-002 abandoned because its val split is spent and re-reading it would be the same error again.

claim: Ensemble members must be scoped to the current experiment, not just the frozen dataset
note: Two experiments share a frozen_sha256 by construction, so that filter alone never separates them.

claim: Validation 0.8462 vs CV 0.8190 on 143 rows -- the gap is within noise, not evidence of improvement
note: 143 rows carries roughly +/-4%. A 0.027 gap is well inside that; reading it as a real gain would be exactly the mistake these splits exist to prevent.

claim: Training on 569 rows instead of 712 costs roughly 0.006-0.010 CV
note: Best single fell 0.8287 (712 rows, exp-001) -> 0.8225 (569 rows, exp-002/3). That is the price of a per-experiment val split, and it is worth paying.

claim: Widening HGB with min_samples_leaf / l2_regularization / max_depth does not measurably help
note: Same split, same folds: wide grid 0.8189 vs old grid (control) 0.8155, +0.0035 against a ~0.017 fold std. The winner chose LESS regularisation than default (min_samples_leaf=10, l2=0, no depth cap), so the regularisation hypothesis is not supported either way.

claim: Cross-experiment CV deltas are dominated by the split, not the technique
note: HGB rose 0.8014 (exp-003) -> 0.8189 (exp-004), but the same-split control accounts for all but 0.0035 of that; gradient_boosting, extra_trees and logistic also rose 0.005-0.012 with no change. Compare techniques within one experiment via a control row, never across experiments.

claim: Validation 0.8671 vs CV 0.8190 on 143 rows is noise, and measures random_forest, not the lever under test
note: SE on 143 rows ~0.032, so +0.048 is ~1.5 SE. Above the ~0.85 suspect line, but the model is an unchanged RF and make leakage is clean. Second experiment running with val > CV (exp-003 +0.027); worth watching, not yet a pattern.

claim: evaluate scores whichever model has the best CV, so the val read often does not test the experiment's change
note: exp-004 changed HGB; evaluate scored RF (0.81896 vs HGB 0.81894). A per-experiment val read is only diagnostic of the lever if it scores the changed model, or the experiment pre-declares which model it is testing.

claim: explore is not experiment-aware: it charts all 712 working rows, including the open experiment's val rows
note: Skipped explore in exp-004 for this reason. Harmless while features are fixed in code, but any feature chosen from explore output would have seen val rows.

claim: None of 24 row-wise engineered features (age/fare bins, one-hot Pclass, Sex x class, ticket/cabin/name parsing, family flags) improves random_forest by >= 0.003 when added to the 12 baseline features
note: Best add: TitleFine +0.0012 +/- 0.0030 SE; 19 of 24 adds were negative, worst TicketPrefix and CabinSide -0.0064. Paired 5x3 CV on identical folds. Refutes 'more features help this RF', not 'these features carry no signal' -- see the redundancy finding.

claim: Title, Pclass, FamilySize and Embarked carry most of the signal for random_forest; Title is the single most valuable feature
note: Removal costs: Title 0.0152 +/- 0.0052 (2.9 SE), FamilySize 0.0070 +/- 0.0025 (2.8 SE), Pclass 0.0094 +/- 0.0049, Embarked 0.0082 +/- 0.0047, Fare 0.0058, Sex 0.0053 +/- 0.0048 (Sex is largely redundant with Title).

claim: Pruning the RF to 6 features (Sex, Pclass, Fare, Embarked, FamilySize, Title) improves on the 12-feature baseline
note: CV 0.8360 -> 0.8401 (+0.0041), but each of the 6 drops (Age, SibSp, Parch, IsAlone, Deck, AgeMissing) was within ~2 SE and accepted greedily, so the gain is partly selection on noise. Val 0.8112 on 143 rows (SE ~0.033) is 0.029 below CV -- first experiment with val < CV -- and cannot distinguish the pruned set from the baseline, which was not val-scored.

claim: Add-one tests against a frozen random_forest are biased against redundant encodings: with max_features='sqrt' fixed, an extra correlated column dilutes how often the strong ones are sampled per split
note: Would explain 19/24 negative adds and why dropping redundant Age/SibSp/Parch helped. Test: re-run the best candidates (TitleFine, AgeClass, WomanOrChild) as SWAPS for the column they refine, or with max_features re-tuned per feature set.

claim: Encoding and bucketing (one-hot Pclass, AgeBin, FareBin, interactions) should be tested on logistic / SVC, not a tree model
note: Trees are invariant to monotone transforms and split ordinals themselves, so this experiment tested bucketing and one-hot on the model least able to benefit. Linear models cannot express a non-monotone age effect without bins.

claim: Features that need fitted state were not tested: Age imputed by Title median, ticket-group size, within-fold family/ticket survival rates
note: All require fitting inside each CV fold (a custom transformer in the Pipeline). Group survival rates are target-derived and leak across folds if computed outside them; Rule 4 is not at issue because nothing external is joined.

claim: Greedy feature selection against a 0.003 bar does not generalise at n=569: the search carries more selection bias (+0.0105) than the CV gain it buys (+0.0043), and generalises 0.0088 +/- 0.0068 worse than not searching at all
note: Nested CV, 5 outer folds, both arms on identical outer folds: arm A re-runs the same features.greedy_search inside each fold, arm B is the fixed 12-feature baseline. nested(search) 0.8296 vs nested(baseline) 0.8384; reported cv 0.8401 minus nested 0.8296 = selection bias +0.0105, positive as nesting requires. -1.29 sigma, so the sign is not certain at 2 SE, but the point estimate is negative and it was pre-registered to land in [-0.010, +0.002]. Hyperparameters were held fixed, so this is the bias of the feature search alone, over a candidate list trimmed to 8. SUPERSEDES the inconclusive claim that pruning to 6 features improves on the baseline: it does not, and the question was always answerable by CV rather than by the val read it was blamed on. Retires the class 'try another feature search'.

claim: The 0.003 bar is about one standard error and 1.7 flipped predictions on 569 rows, so a single add/remove verdict near it is close to a coin flip
note: Measured, not assumed: four comparisons re-run under 10 fold seeds on exp-006's 569 training rows (750 fits, 42s). Seed-to-seed sd of the paired delta 0.0024-0.0041, i.e. 0.77-1.37x the naive SE this repo reports -- so the naive SE is approximately honest and the Nadeau-Bengio x2.18 resampled-t correction is too conservative for a fully paired statistic. The bar lands at 0.73-1.23 sigma. Separately, the add rule is biased against acceptance before any candidate is seen: the 24 adds centre at -0.0022 with sd 0.0021, so a feature needs a true effect of +0.0052 for 50% acceptance and +0.0070 for 80%. The advertised 0.003 bar is in practice a 0.005-0.007 bar, which is how 'none of 24 candidates cleared 0.003' should be read.

claim: An asymmetric removal rule ratchets: a feature whose true cost is under the bar is always dropped, and nothing can add it back
note: Arithmetic from exp-006's own rows, not a model. Three of the six accepted drops cost accuracy -- Parch -0.0012, Deck -0.0047, AgeMissing -0.0023 -- and were accepted only because the cost failed to reach +0.003. Age went on +0.0024 +/- 0.0028, i.e. 1.3 passengers. The six sum to exactly +0.00410, the entire published gain, which is therefore Deck (+0.0047) and AgeMissing (+0.0023) and nothing else. Combined with a one-sigma bar, every undecidable removal goes the same way, so the errors accumulate instead of cancelling. Untried fix: drop only when the measured cost is <= 0, or require the cumulative prune to clear the bar against the original baseline.

claim: Cross-experiment comparison of absolute CV scores is invalid here: identical configurations have drifted 0.004-0.011 between experiments, one to three times the effects being argued about
note: Measured from the ledger across exp-002/003/004 (and exp-006 for random_forest), 12-feature tune rows, re-tuned per experiment: gradient_boosting sd 0.0098, hist_gradient_boosting 0.0107, random_forest 0.0097 (range 0.0211 over four), logistic 0.0044, svc 0.0021. open_experiment re-draws the split each time, so these comparisons are unpaired. This is the programme's most likely failure mode and is NOT yet fixed: each experiment is internally paired and defensible while every comparison between them is made at 2-3x the effect size. Untried fix: a persisted champion, re-scored on each experiment's own folds, with delta_vs_champion in the ledger instead of an absolute CV.

claim: The validation read is an integrity tripwire with ~0.06 resolution, not a calibrator of selection bias
note: 143 rows: SE 0.032, and accuracy moves in steps of 1/143 = 0.0070, so a true 0.004 difference cannot appear as 0.004. Paired reads reach ~0.06; Thresholdout's own noise at this n has sd 0.020. A split able to adjudicate 0.004 needs ~59,000 rows. The cv->val gaps recorded so far are +0.0272 (exp-003), +0.0481 (exp-004), -0.0289 (exp-006): mean +0.0155, sd 0.0398, so the point estimate says selection DEFLATES cv, which it does not. Reading exp-006's -0.0289 as the check firing correctly was confirmation bias. Resolving a 0.010 bias through this gap would take ~60 experiments. What 143 rows do catch is a 0.064 defect, which is how exp-002's contamination was found. SUPERSEDES the framing in exp-006's inconclusive finding.
